alex: hey all — alex here, first day on runtime. trying to build from source on ubuntu 22.04 with an RTX A2000. make aborts with nvcc link errors. anyone got the minimal local setup steps?

maria: welcome! quick q: are you using our dev container or building on host? also pinging @devon from infra.

alex: building on host for now. error snippet: ```/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc -ccbin g++ -o libinference.so ... /tmp/ccXYZ.o: In function `__device_stub__Z...': undefined reference to `__cudaRegister...` collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status```

devon: @alex — that looks like an nvcc/driver/toolkit mismatch or a g++ ABI issue. steps we give to new hires: 1) check nvidia-smi (driver) 2) use matching CUDA toolkit (we test against 12.1) 3) use GCC 9.x (we pin to 9.5 in CI) 4) prefer the dev container if you can: `docker run --gpus all -it redwood/runtime-dev:2025-09 bash`

alex: i ran nvidia-smi, driver shows 525.85, cuda driver compatibility 12.x — hmm

samir: extra gotcha: kernel headers missing cause compilation oddities. `sudo apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r)` if you see injector errors. Also if you built CUDA toolkit from runfile, ensure `/usr/local/cuda` points to the right toolkit. `ls -l /usr/local/cuda`

julia: also watch out for host g++ version. nvcc often links against libstdc++ from the toolkit; we ask devs to `update-alternatives` to g++-9 when building. if you see undefined refs to device regs it's usually nvcc/gcc mismatch.

devon: if you want to keep host, this command sequence usually fixes it: ```sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y gcc-9 g++-9 linux-headers-$(uname -r) sudo ln -sfn /usr/bin/gcc-9 /usr/local/bin/gcc && sudo ln -sfn /usr/bin/g++-9 /usr/local/bin/g++ export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.1 export PATH=$CUDA_HOME/bin:$PATH export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$CUDA_HOME/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH make clean && make -j8 CUDAVERSION=12.1```

maria: we also maintain an internal troubleshooting doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/runtime-build (search "local build"). If you can, try the container first — it mirrors CI so fewer surprises.

alex: tried the container — build started and passed the early linking step. will finish full build but looks promising. thanks! :tada:

ops-bot: welcome alex — added to #runtime-onboarding checklist (task: complete local build).

alex: quick followup: once i switch to g++-9 i hit an issue with CUB/THRUST includes. any preferred inc paths?

samir: use the toolkit includes by setting `CUDAPATH=$CUDA_HOME/include` and ensure `-I$CUDAPATH` is before system include flags. our `scripts/setup_dev.sh --cuda 12.1` handles this for you.

julia: if you run into quant kernel compile errors, ping me — I can share the small patches we apply locally.

alex: great — container + setup script did the trick. I'm past link errors and running tests. huge thanks everyone. :rocket:
